results.fact: Elevation gain of the Bedal Creek approach-variant round trip
results.evidence: The variant's own notes say its distance and gain are the full round trip by the Bedal Creek line to the summit, not to the 5,800 ft ridge; a published Bedal trailhead account gives exactly 5,300 ft and 9.5 mi round trip and other reports give 5,500-6,500 ft, so 5,300 is a sourced figure, not a copy of the saddle elevation. gain_ft 5935 (=7,835-1,900, the Cougar Creek trailhead) is a whole-route figure within the reported range and is not settled by agreeing sources, so it is left alone.

results.fact: Climbing season window (does it include September?)
results.evidence: Five fields on the row (best_season, seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow, monthBreakdown.September 'good', climate.bySeason.summer 'Jul-Sep', approach_variants[0].season 'Jul-Sep') treat September as in-season; only the season chip says Jul-Aug. Externally, Corkscrew ascents are documented in September (a Sept 2025 car-to-car trip report) and the peak's season is described as running into early fall with the glacier deteriorating late; one Bedal account calls Jul-Aug optimal, which the row already expresses as the most reliable stretch.

results.fact: Number of technical pitches on the route
results.correct_value: 8 pitches (P7 60 m 5.10, P8 30 m 5.8 flake traverse to the heather ledge)
results.evidence: The route's topo lists 8 pitches, with P7 at 60 m and P8 a 30 m 5.8 flake traverse to the heather ledge; a 2023 CascadeClimbers trip report is titled '8 pitches, 5.10+', and the FA report's own pitch tally comes to about eight. The row's 7-row breakdown merges P7 and P8 into a single 90 m 'pitch 7', which the row's single 60 m rope cannot lead, so the breakdown is split and the five '7 pitches' prose copies are aligned with pitches=8, beta, itinerary and timing. Two other accounts count 7, having linked or skipped the traverse.

patches.fact: Number of technical pitches on the route

expect.notes: Steep, left-leaning corner-and-chimney system with 5.9 climbing low; the crux comes near the top where the crack arches left and turns slightly overhanging, but gear protection is excellent throughout.
Sustained, varied pitch linking a hand crack, featured face holds, and a short rightward hand traverse to an overhanging crack section below a horizontal roof.
Right-facing corner to a giant heather ledge; several similar-looking corners sit nearby, making this a route-finding pitch as much as a climbing one.
Left-trending crack system toward a pedestal; parties have reported some ambiguity near the top, so favor the leftward line rather than the most obvious crack.
Knob-and-fin face climbing (a bit runout, roughly 5.8R) leads into a right-facing corner that gives this pitch its own hard, near-crux moves.
Featured, juggy face climbing to another large heather ledge — a breather before the final pitch.

Climbs past a gendarme/prow on hand cracks and positive edges, then traverses left across fun flakes to the final heather ledge where technical climbing ends and the shared Corkscrew scramble to the summit begins.
expect.anchor: Gear (heather ledge, top of technical climbing)
